public_rationale: The report can be inspected, but the whole statement lacks a stable test. It combines a personal qualification with undefined terms: real and imminent. The report contains discussion of current AI, a prospective transition to superintelligence, and policy proposals. Treating the existence of those proposals as a refutation would be unfair; treating uncertainty about superintelligence as proof of Marcus's entire statement would also overreach.
limitations: This does not endorse OpenAI's expectations about superintelligence.
It does not establish that superintelligence existed or was imminent on April 6.
A narrower claim about demonstrated capabilities could be assessable, but would not preserve the full wording.

from_speaker: Today’s new OpenAI report on Superintelligence

our_interpretation: The statement expresses a qualified assessment of the report's subject matter.
Something real could refer to existing superintelligence, present AI effects, or actionable policy proposals. These readings have different tests.
Imminent supplies no time window. Assigning one would create a commitment Marcus did not make.
The phrase as far as I can tell is an epistemic qualification, not a conditional forecast antecedent.
No single sufficiently clear reading of the whole statement supports a fair binary assessment.
criteria.support_condition: No stable condition can be specified without first choosing what real refers to and supplying a meaning and time window for imminent.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No stable condition can be specified for the whole statement. Existing AI applications or concrete policy proposals would not necessarily contradict a claim about superintelligence's availability.
